cohort: 83,019 infants in the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS)
finding: Infants delivered by cesarean section did not have a significantly different frequency of bowel movements or prevalence of constipation at 1 year old compared to those delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Infants delivered by cesarean section were not at increased risk for constipation at one year old compared to those delivered vaginally.
